questions.question: R varies directly as S and inversely as T. When R = { {2} over 3} and T = { {5} over 7}, S = { {4} over 21}. Find S when R = { {3} over 4} and T = { {1} over 9}.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R varies directly as S and inversely as T.

When R = { {2} over 3} and T = { {5} over 7}, S = { {4} over 21}. 

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

R ∝ S and R ∝ (1)/(T)

Therefore, 

R ∝ (S)/(T)

⇒ R = (kS)/(T)

Now, on substituting the value of the respective variable in the above formula, we get,

⇒ (2)/(3) = k(frac{4)/(21)}{(5)/(7)}

⇒ (2)/(3) = k(4)/(15)

⇒ k = (5)/(2)

Now, 

⇒ R = (kS)/(T)

The above-obtained formula can be written as:

⇒ S = (RT)/(k)

⇒ S = (frac{3)/(4) times (1)/(9)}{(5)/(2)}

⇒ S = (frac{1)/(12)}{(5)/(2)}

⇒ S = (1)/(30)

∴ The required value of S is (1)/(30).

questions.question: What will be the compound interest on a sum of ₹ 15,000 at the interest rate of 8% per annum in one year, interest compounded semi-annually?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **semi-annual compounding**, the rate becomes 8% ÷ 2 = 4% and time periods n = 2.

Effective **Interest Rate** for 2 periods = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

**Compound Interest** = 15,000 × 8.16% = 15,000 × 0.0816 = 1,224.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,224.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹ 15,000

**Annual Rate (R)** = 8%

**Time (T)** = 1 year

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ; Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa119948ab3f7bfc4676af1a06b6a4ba91e56745ddf72fe9e96119b9265a86f7.png] 

Since interest is **compounded semi-annually**:

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 8% ÷ 2 = 4%

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 1 year × 2 = 2

⇒ A = 15,000 × (1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 15,000 × (1.04)²

⇒ A = 15,000 × 1.0816

⇒ A = 16,224

⇒ CI = 16,224 − 15,000

⇒ CI = 1,224

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,224.**

**__Additional Information__**

Semi-annual Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the **annual rate** is divided by 2 and the **time** in years is multiplied by 2.

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive periods with rate r%, the **effective rate** is given by the formula: r + r + (r²/100)%.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 periods is P × (r/100)². In this case, the difference is 15,000 × (4/100)² = ₹ 24.

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹16,956 in 4 years and to ₹19,116 in 6{ {1} over 2} years at a certain rate percent per annum, interest being simple in both cases. The rate of interest p.a. is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 2.5 years = 19,116 − 16,956 = ₹2,160

**Interest per year** = 2,160 ÷ 2.5 = ₹864

Principal = 16,956 − (864 × 4) = 16,956 − 3,456 = ₹13,500

**Rate of interest** = (864 ÷ 13,500) × 100 = 6.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after 4 years (A₁) = ₹16,956

**Amount** after 6.5 years (A₂) = ₹19,116

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f051a9b7dce5c589a95ae504cbbc469f06b3f17ce1d588f8b2a5ccec852be1d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for (6.5 − 4) years = 19,116 − 16,956

⇒ Interest for 2.5 years = ₹2,160

⇒ Interest for 1 year = 2,160 ÷ 2.5 = ₹864

⇒ Interest for 4 years = 864 × 4 = ₹3,456

⇒ Principal (P) = A₁ − SI for 4 years

⇒ P = 16,956 − 3,456 = ₹13,500

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (864 × 100) ÷ 13,500

⇒ R = 864 ÷ 135 = 6.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Properties

In simple interest, the interest remains constant for every time period as it is always calculated on the original **Principal** amount.

Direct Rate Calculation

Rate R = (Interest × 100) ÷ (P × T). If T = 1 year, then R = (Interest for 1 year ÷ P) × 100.

Amount Formula

Total Amount A = P (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100), where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and T is time in years.

questions.question: The cost price and selling price of rice are the same. Due to a faulty weighing machine, the seller earns a 15% profit. If Rs. x is the cost price of 1000 gm rice and the machine is changed which shows 1000 gm instead of 950 gm, what should be the selling price (in Rs.) now to get the same percentage of profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To maintain a **15% profit** when the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are technically the same per unit, the total SP must be 1.15 × Total CP.

Current scenario: Machine shows **1000 gm** but gives **950 gm**. The effective CP for the dealer is the cost of 950 gm.

Effective CP = (950 ÷ 1000) × x = **0.95x**.

Required Profit = 15%. Formula: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

New SP = 0.95x × 1.15 = **1.0925x**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.0925x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Cost price of 1000 gm = **Rs. x**. Machine shows 1000 gm for an actual weight of **950 gm**. Desired Profit = **15%**.
Formulas: Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100 | SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b537a3a183b230f8f9a417b103d93123d18e27aa1d672cf67fca92bb36b41e7.png] 
⇒ Cost price of 1 gm = x ÷ 1000.
⇒ When machine shows 1000 gm, the actual quantity is 950 gm.
⇒ Actual CP for the dealer for 1000 gm shown = (x ÷ 1000) × 950 = **0.95x**.
⇒ To earn 15% profit on this transaction: SP = 0.95x × (115 ÷ 100).
⇒ SP = 0.95x × 1.15 = **1.0925x**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.0925x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit is generated either by increasing the selling price or by reducing the actual weight delivered. Gain% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Effective Profit Percentage

If a dealer sells at k% profit but uses a weight that is w% less, Total Profit% = [(k + w) ÷ (100 − w)] × 100.</p

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral In PQRS ∠P is opposite to ∠R. If ∠P and ∠R are 3x + 5 and 4x respectively, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **cyclic quadrilateral**, the sum of **opposite angles** is always 180°.

Given: ∠P + ∠R = 180°

⇒ (3x + 5) + 4x = 180

⇒ 7x + 5 = 180

⇒ 7x = 175

⇒ x = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠P = 3x + 5

∠R = 4x

Quadrilateral PQRS is **cyclic**, where P and R are **opposite vertices**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/433e6eaf7b464fdf7644f7bbe69261fdc3a75e3c83fe35a0470096297595311c.png] 

According to the **Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorem**, the sum of either pair of **opposite angles** is 180°.

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 180°

⇒ (3x + 5) + 4x = 180

⇒ 7x + 5 = 180

⇒ 7x = 180 − 5

⇒ 7x = 175

⇒ x = 175 ÷ 7

⇒ x = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is cyclic if and only if its vertices lie on a circle, and its opposite angles sum to 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Ptolemy's Theorem

For a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of the opposite sides: (PQ × RS) + (QR × PS) = PR × QS.</p

questions.question: Anil is 12.5 percent more efficient than Sachin. If Sachin alone can finish a work in 10 days, then in how many days will Anil alone finish the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency: Anil is 12.5% (1/8) more efficient than Sachin → Efficiency ratio Anil : Sachin = 9 : 8

Time ratio (Anil : Sachin) = 8 : 9 (Inverse of Efficiency ratio)

Given Sachin takes 10 days → 9 units = 10 days

Anil alone will take → 8 units = (10 ÷ 9) × 8 = 80/9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 80/9 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Sachin alone finishes in 10 days. Anil is 112.5% as efficient as Sachin.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Let Sachin efficiency = 8 units/day

⇒ Anil efficiency = 8 + (12.5% of 8) = 9 units/day

questions.question:
Simplify the following: 

 (3)/(2)times (11)/(5)div ((25)/(44)times (11)/(5))div (33)/(15)=?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simplify: (3)/(2) times (11)/(5) div ((25)/(44) times (11)/(5)) div (33)/(15)

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Simplify the expression inside the parentheses:

(25)/(44) times (11)/(5) = (25 times 11)/(44 times 5) = (275)/(220) = (5)/(4)

Step 2: The expression now becomes:

(3)/(2) times (11)/(5) div (5)/(4) div (33)/(15)

Step 3: Simplify the division operations:

(11)/(5) div (5)/(4) = (11)/(5) times (4)/(5) = (44)/(25)

Step 4: The expression now becomes:

(3)/(2) times (44)/(25) div (33)/(15)

Step 5: Simplify the next division:

(44)/(25) div (33)/(15) = (44)/(25) times (15)/(33) = (44 times 15)/(25 times 33) = (660)/(825) = (4)/(5)

Step 6: Final multiplication:

(3)/(2) times (4)/(5) = (12)/(10) = (6)/(5)

**∴ The simplified value is (6)/(5).**

Increase in her speed (b) = 4 km/h

1st time late (t₁) = 30 min

2ⁿd time late (t₂) = 10 min

D = (t₁ – t₂) (a + b)a/b

**Calculation:**

According to the formula:

Required Distance = (t₁ – t₂) (a + b)a/b

⇒ (30 - 10)/60 × (20 + 4) × 20/4

⇒ 20/60 × 24 × 20/4

⇒ 1/3 × 24 × 5

⇒ 8 × 5

⇒ 40 km.

**∴**** the distance between the tuition classes from her home is 40 km.**

questions.question: Let P be an interior point of a right-angled isosceles triangle ABC with hypotenuse AB. If the perpendicular distance of P from each of AB, BC, and CA is 4(√2 − 1) cm, then the area, in sq cm, of the triangle ABC is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, the point equidistant from all three sides is the **incenter**, and the distance is the **inradius (r)**.

For a right-angled isosceles triangle with leg **a** and hypotenuse **a√2**, the inradius is given by: **r = (2a − a√2) ÷ 2**.

⇒ 4(√2 − 1) = a(2 − √2) ÷ 2

⇒ 8(√2 − 1) = a√2(√2 − 1)

⇒ a = 8 ÷ √2 = 4√2 cm.

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × a² = (1 ÷ 2) × (4√2)² = (1 ÷ 2) × 32 = 16 sq cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 sq cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Triangle **ABC** is a right-angled isosceles triangle with hypotenuse **AB**.

⇒ Let legs **AC = BC = a** cm. Then hypotenuse **AB = a√2** cm.

⇒ Perpendicular distance of point **P** from each side = 4(√2 − 1) cm.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Inradius **r** of a right triangle = (Base + Height − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2

⇒ Area of triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35fe7351af66a34bfd8629603e95f17961337c7b811e6f8b296b47533737448b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Point **P** is equidistant from all sides, so **P** is the incenter and the distance is the inradius **r**.

⇒ r = (a + a − a√2) ÷ 2

⇒ 4(√2 − 1) = (2a − a√2) ÷ 2

⇒ 8(√2 − 1) = a(2 − √2)

⇒ 8(√2 − 1) = a × √2(√2 − 1)

⇒ a = 8 ÷ √2

⇒ a = 4√2 cm

⇒ Area of ▵ABC = (1 ÷ 2) × a × a

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × (4√2) × (4√2)

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 32

⇒ Area = 16 sq cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 sq cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incenter Properties

The incenter is the point of concurrency of the angle bisectors and is equidistant from all sides of the triangle.

Inradius and Area

The relation between Area (A), semi-perimeter (s), and inradius (r) is A = r × s.

Right Triangle Inradius

For any right triangle with legs p, q and hypotenuse h, the inradius r = (p + q − h) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12(1)/(2) hours and 25 hours, respectively. The pipes were opened simultaneously, and it was found that, due to leakage in the bottom, it took one hour 40 minutes more to fill the cistern. If the cistern is full, in how much time (in hours) will the leak alone empty 70% of the cistern?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12.5, 25) = 25 units. Efficiencies: A = 2, B = 1. Total = 3 units/hr.

Normal time = 25 ÷ 3 hours = 8 hours 20 mins. Time with leak = 8h 20m + 1h 40m = 10 hours.

New efficiency (A + B − Leak) = 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5. Thus, Leak Efficiency = 3 − 2.5 = 0.5 units/hr.

Time to empty 70% capacity = (25 × 0.7) ÷ 0.5 = 17.5 ÷ 0.5 = 35 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 12.5 hours = 25/2 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 25 hours

Extra time due to leak = 1 hour 40 minutes = 1 + 40/60 = 5/3 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of Pipes A and B = 2 + 1 = 3 units/hr

⇒ Normal time taken to fill the cistern = 25 ÷ 3 hours = 8 hours 20 minutes

⇒ Total time taken with leakage = 8 hours 20 minutes + 1 hour 40 minutes = 10 hours

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B − Leak) = Total Work ÷ Total Time = 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of the Leak = (Efficiency of A + B) − (Combined Efficiency with Leak)

Negative Efficiency

In pipes and cisterns, a leak or an outlet pipe is treated as a component with negative efficiency because it removes work (water) from the system.

Work-Time Relationship

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time. When work is constant, efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the task.

Net Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and leak L empties in y hours, the net rate of filling is (1/x − 1/y) per hour.</p

questions.question: A car owner buys gasoline at Rs. 17, Rs. 19 & Rs. 21 per liter for three consecutive years. Compute the average cost per liter, if he spends Rs. 6783 per year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average cost is the total money spent divided by the total quantity bought.

Total amount spent = 3 × 6783 = Rs. 20349

Total quantity = (6783 ÷ 17) + (6783 ÷ 19) + (6783 ÷ 21) = 399 + 357 + 323 = 1079 liters

Average cost = 20349 ÷ 1079 ≈ Rs. 18.85

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 18.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount spent per year = Rs. 6783

Prices per liter for 3 consecutive years = Rs. 17, Rs. 19, and Rs. 21

**Formula Used:**

Average Cost = Total Amount Spent ÷ Total Quantity

 Total Quantity = 1079 L

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total amount spent in 3 years = 6783 × 3 = Rs. 20349

⇒ Quantity bought in 1st year = 6783 ÷ 17 = 399 liters

⇒ Quantity bought in 2nd year = 6783 ÷ 19 = 357 liters

⇒ Quantity bought in 3rd year = 6783 ÷ 21 = 323 liters

⇒ Total quantity of gasoline = 399 + 357 + 323 = 1079 liters

⇒ Average cost per liter = 20349 ÷ 1079

⇒ Average cost per liter = 18.859...

⇒ Average cost per liter ≈ Rs. 18.85

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 18.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Harmonic Mean for Averages

When a constant total amount is spent on items with varying prices, the overall average price is derived using the Harmonic Mean of the individual prices: Average = n ÷ (1/a + 1/b + 1/c ...).

Average Speed Analogy

This concept is strictly identical to calculating average speed when equal distances are covered at different speeds (since Speed = Distance ÷ Time mathematically equals Price = Amount ÷ Quantity).

Weighted Average

If varying amounts were spent across the different years, the general formula directly applies: Weighted Average = (Amount₁ + Amount₂ + ...) ÷ (Quantity₁ + Quantity₂ + ...).

questions.question: ​In a trapezium, one diagonal divides the other in the ratio 2 ∶ 7. If the length of the larger of the two parallel sides is 42 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the other parallel side?

In a trapezium, the ratio of the lengths of the parallel sides is equal to the ratio in which the diagonals divide each other.

Ratio of parallel sides = Ratio of diagonal segments = 2 : 7

Given larger parallel side (7 parts) = 42 cm

1 part = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 cm

Smaller parallel side (2 parts) = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of segments of diagonals = 2 : 7

Length of larger parallel side = 42 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a trapezium ABCD with AB || CD and diagonals intersecting at O, ΔAOB ∼ ΔCOD (by AAA similarity). Therefore, AB/CD = AO/CO = BO/DO.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0bc95316f13ec4c80cc1e230d0e53eea2682e442f8315bd8d984dd4970892ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the parallel sides be a and b, where b = 42 cm.

⇒ According to the similarity property: a / b = 2 / 7

⇒ a / 42 = 2 / 7

⇒ a = (2 × 42) ÷ 7

⇒ a = 2 × 6

⇒ a = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is calculated as 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × height, or Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is called the median, and its length is the average of the parallel sides: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Similarity Property

The triangles formed by the intersection of diagonals and the parallel sides (top and bottom triangles) are always similar by AAA criteria because of alternate interior angles.</p

questions.question: 27⁵ + 3¹³ is divisible by
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert 27 to base 3: 27⁵ = (3³)⁵ = 3¹⁵

Expression: 3¹⁵ + 3¹³

Factor out the lowest power: 3¹³(3² + 1)

Simplify the bracket: 3¹³ × (9 + 1) = 3¹³ × 10

The result is a multiple of 10, thus it is divisible by 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

27⁵ + 3¹³

**Formula Used:**

(am)ⁿ = am × ⁿ

am + aⁿ = aⁿ(am−ⁿ + 1), where m > n

**Calculation:**

⇒ 27⁵ + 3¹³

⇒ (3³)⁵ + 3¹³

⇒ 3¹⁵ + 3¹³

⇒ 3¹³(3¹⁵−¹³ + 1)

⇒ 3¹³(3² + 1)

⇒ 3¹³(9 + 1)

⇒ 3¹³ × 10

⇒ Since 10 is a factor of the resulting expression, it must be divisible by 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

Laws of Indices

Key rules include am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ and (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ, which allow simplification of large exponential terms to a common base.

Divisibility Rule of 10

A number is divisible by 10 if its units digit is 0. Any integer multiplied by 10 results in a number divisible by 10.

Factoring Exponential Expressions

When adding or subtracting powers of the same base, always factor out the term with the lowest exponent to simplify the constant factor.</p

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is twice its breadth. If its length is decreased by 4 cm and breadth is increased by 4 cm, the area of the rectangle increases by 52 cm². The length of the rectangle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **breadth** be x, then **length** is 2x.

New Area − Old Area = 52

(2x − 4)(x + 4) − 2x² = 52

2x² + 8x − 4x − 16 − 2x² = 52 ⇒ 4x = 68 ⇒ x = 17 cm.

**Length** = 2 × 17 = 34 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length (L)** = 2 × **Breadth (B)**

New length = L − 4

New breadth = B + 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ac89172e9c71ca2f00293e89aeccce61d65bd3e375f463438f540f3fe56bd2b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original Area = L × B = 2B × B = 2B²

⇒ New Area = (2B − 4) × (B + 4)

⇒ (2B − 4)(B + 4) = 2B² + 52

⇒ 2B² + 8B − 4B − 16 = 2B² + 52

⇒ 4B − 16 = 52

⇒ 4B = 68

⇒ B = 17 cm

⇒ Length = 2 × 17 = 34 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The area is the product of its **length** and **breadth** (Area = L × B).

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total boundary length is given by 2 × (L + B).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is √(L² + B²).</p

questions.question: Which of the given number is NOT divisible by 3?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the **sum of digits** for each number.

If the **sum is divisible by 3**, the number is divisible by 3.

Option 1: 6+8+7 = 21 (Divisible by 3)

Option 2: 7+1+3 = 11 (**NOT divisible by 3**)

**∴ The correct answer is 713.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 687, 713, 927, 453.

**Formula Used:** **Divisibility rule of 3** states that a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: **687** → 6 + 8 + 7 = 21. Since 21 ÷ 3 = 7, it is divisible.

⇒ Case 2: **713** → 7 + 1 + 3 = 11. Since 11 is **not divisible** by 3, 713 is not divisible.

⇒ Case 3: **927** → 9 + 2 + 7 = 18. Since 18 ÷ 3 = 6, it is divisible.

⇒ Case 4: **453** → 4 + 5 + 3 = 12. Since 12 ÷ 3 = 4, it is divisible.

**∴ The correct answer is 713.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

Similar to 3, a number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is **simultaneously divisible** by both 2 (even number) and 3 (sum of digits rule).

Prime Numbers

713 is not divisible by 3, but it is a composite number (23 × 31 = 713).</p

A dog takes 5 leaps for every 6 leaps of a hare, but 4 leaps of the dog are equal to 5 leaps of the hare. The ratio of the speed of dog and hare is?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Write the **number of leaps** for both animals in the first row and their **leap equivalence** in the second row.

**Dog** : 5 leaps | **Hare** : 6 leaps

Equivalence: 4 Dog leaps = 5 Hare leaps

To find the **Speed Ratio**, cross-multiply the number of leaps with the opposite animal's equivalence factor.

Speed Ratio = (5 × 5) : (6 × 4) = 25 : 24

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of leaps: **Dog** = 5, **Hare** = 6

Leap distance ratio: 4 **Dog leaps** = 5 **Hare leaps**

**Formula Used:**

**Speed** = (Number of leaps in given time) × (Distance covered in each leap)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8f3d426b0e51aff3b1af7fcfdba9f2b8838ad59f5bc612436dafa9349048cfb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance of 1 **Dog leap** be D and 1 **Hare leap** be H.

⇒ According to the question: 4 × D = 5 × H

⇒ D / H = 5 / 4

⇒ Speed of **Dog** (Sd) = 5 × D

⇒ Speed of **Hare** (Sₕ) = 6 × H

⇒ Ratio = (Sd) / (Sₕ) = (5 × D) / (6 × H)

⇒ Ratio = (5 / 6) × (D / H)

⇒ Substituting the value of D/H: Ratio = (5 / 6) × (5 / 4)

⇒ Ratio = 25 / 24

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance Relationship

When time is constant, **Speed** is directly proportional to the **Distance** covered. In leap problems, distance depends on both frequency and leap length.

Leap Length Units

If x leaps of A = y leaps of B, then the ratio of their leap lengths is **Length A : Length B = y : x**.

Ratio Multiplication

To find the resultant ratio of speed, always multiply the **Frequency Ratio** by the **Distance Ratio** of each individual step.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days and 48 days, respectively. They work together for 12 days. The remaining work is completed by C alone in 10 days. A and C together can complete 62.5% of the original work in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 36, 48) = 144 units.

Efficiency: **A** = 4, **B** = 3. Combined (**A**+**B**) = 7.

Work done in 12 days = 12 × 7 = 84. Remaining work = 144 − 84 = 60.

**C**'s Efficiency = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day.

62.5% of Original Work = 144 × 5/8 = 90 units.

Time for (**A** + **C**) = 90 ÷ (4 + 6) = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 36 days

Time taken by **B** = 48 days

Common work duration for **A** and **B** = 12 days

Time taken by **C** to finish remaining work = 10 days

 
 

 **Person**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM(36, 48) = 144 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 144 ÷ 48 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (**A** + **B**) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day.

⇒ Work done by **A** and **B** in 12 days = 12 × 7 = 84 units.

⇒ Remaining work for **C** = 144 − 84 = 60 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = Remaining Work ÷ Time = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day.

⇒ 62.5% of the Original Work = 144 × (62.5/100) = 144 × (5/8) = 90 units.

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (**A** + **C**) = 4 + 6 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by (**A** + **C**) to complete 90 units = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. For a constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting common percentages like 62.5% to fractions (5/8) or 37.5% (3/8) simplifies calculation significantly.

Combined Efficiency

When individuals work together, their individual efficiencies are added to find the total rate of work done per day.</p

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/h. The time taken by the boat to go 35 km downstream is 1.25 times the time taken by it to go 14 km upstream. How much time (in hours) will it take to go 60 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The speed of a boat in still water (X) is 10 km/h.

Time taken by the boat to go 35 km downstream is 1.25 times the time taken by it to go 14 km upstream

Distance upstream = 35 km

Distance downstream = 14 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed Upstream = Speed of a boat in still water (X) - Speed of the current (Y) km/h

Speed Downstream = Speed of a boat in still water (X) + Speed of the current (Y) km/h

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

(35)/((10 + Y)) = 1.25 × (14)/(10 - Y)

⇒ (5)/((10 + Y)) = 1.25 × (2)/(10 - Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = .25 × 2 × (10 + Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = .50 × (10 + Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = 5 + .5Y

⇒ 1.5Y = 5

Y = 10/3 km/h.

Now, Speed downstream = 10 + 10/3 = 40/3 km/h

Time taken for 60 km downstream = (60)/(40/3)

⇒ 9/2

⇒ 4.5 h

**∴ The time (in hours) it will take to go 60 km downstream is 4.5**.
